releases.name: v0.5.4 — AI Studio backend v0.2.14
releases.body:
Move the managed AI Studio backend to upstream v0.2.14 (`v0.2.14-magpie.1`).

- Fixes from upstream: sign-in no longer loses credentials when closing Camoufox fails; Camoufox child processes no longer linger on Windows; `limit: 0` cooldowns back off instead of waiting out RetryDelay; Chrome account import is more reliable.
- The managed build now uses upstream's own distributor setting instead of a patch: the admin page says updates are managed by magpie-gemini-web, and the update endpoint refuses with HTTP 409 (was 403).
- Upstream's new `MODEL_CHANNELS`, `MEDIA_OUTPUT` and `MEDIA_BASE_URL` settings belong to the admin page and are not taken from the environment the plugin runs in.

**Upgrading:** a backend installed by an earlier plugin version is replaced automatically on the next start, keeping accounts, port and sign-in credentials. Camoufox is not downloaded again.

**Note:** upstream now accepts the AI Studio terms of service on an account's behalf, when its model list is read, if the account hasn't accepted them yet.

Rolling back to v0.5.3 keeps working: the new version's data changes are additive.

Validation: all five platform CI jobs rebuild the backend and match the pinned SHA-256s, and run the real-binary managed smoke test. With real Google accounts: an existing v0.2.13 setup upgraded and served requests, rolled back to v0.2.13 and served requests, and a new account signed in through the plugin's one-click flow and served a request.

The attached npm tarball is the same artifact published to npm.

releases.name: AI Studio 0.2.14-magpie.1 — Upstream-managed updates
releases.body:
AI Studio backend based on upstream v0.2.14, managed exclusively by the Magpie plugin.

- Built with upstream's own distributor settings instead of a patch (`-X internal/app.version=v0.2.14-magpie.1`, `-X internal/app.managedBy=magpie-gemini-web`). Update checks return local managed status without contacting GitHub; installing an update returns HTTP 409 without changing files or restarting.
- The admin version panel says updates are managed by magpie-gemini-web.
- Command-line build (no `desktop` tag), as before.
- Include five SHA-256-pinned platform archives, upstream MIT license, checksums, and reproducible build metadata.

Source: upstream commit 370a313814099b508881807effa2a9d72f2d7e66 (tag v0.2.14), no patches. Build instructions: docs/studio-release.md.

These are backend assets consumed by magpie-gemini-web v0.5.4, not the npm plugin package.

releases.name: v0.5.3 — AI Studio proxy settings that stick
releases.body:
Fix the managed AI Studio backend ignoring the proxy saved in its admin page and falling back to a stale system proxy (#14).

- The admin page now owns the proxy, timeouts, concurrency and other runtime settings: the plugin writes defaults to `.env` once and no longer overwrites them or passes them over it on start. Only the settings the plugin depends on (listen address, API key, admin credentials, backend recipe) stay plugin-managed.
- `PROXY` is passed only when `studio.proxy` or `AI_STUDIO_PROXY` names one; an empty value counts as unset. A proxy kept in an older `config.json` is migrated to `.env` once.
- The usage card shows the proxy the backend actually uses, where it comes from, whether a saved one is overridden, and whether a change still needs a restart; it also links the local admin page. Sign-in instructions and failures and `studio:status` show the same.
- `studio:start --proxy` saves the proxy to `.env` instead of setting it over the saved one.

**Upgrading:** a backend started by an earlier version keeps an empty `PROXY` in its environment until it restarts. The usage card says so and gives the command; restart it once.

The proxy set for `ai-studio` in Magpie's provider settings is still not passed to the local backend; set it in the admin page or with `studio.proxy`.

Validation: all five platform CI jobs pass (181 tests on macOS/Linux; Windows runs the Studio suite). End-to-end checks against the real v0.2.13-magpie.1 backend cover admin-page saves surviving restarts, a cleared proxy, `studio.proxy` overriding a saved one, and CLI status without a launch record.

The attached npm tarball is the same artifact published to npm.

releases.name: v0.5.2 — Managed AI Studio updates
releases.body:
Upgrade AI Studio to v0.2.13 with a plugin-managed backend, so backend updates follow plugin upgrades consistently across platforms.

- Disable the backend's admin online updater and replace its controls with a message to upgrade through Magpie. Update installation returns HTTP 403; update checks do not contact GitHub.
- Use SHA-256-pinned v0.2.13-magpie.1 builds for macOS x64/arm64, Linux x64/arm64, and Windows x64.
- Set AI Studio's backend timeout and the plugin's default request timeout to 30 minutes for long responses.
- Filter Build/assistant_route models out of the Agent model list.
- Improve process identity checks, stale PID recovery, restart handling, and version-conflict recovery while preserving account/configuration data.
- Include reproducible backend builds, platform CI, and updated Chinese/English documentation.

Validation: all five platform CI jobs pass. macOS/Linux run the full plugin suite (178 tests); Windows runs the complete Studio suite with platform-appropriate checks. Every platform rebuilds the backend, matches the pinned archive/executable SHA-256 hashes, and verifies real installation, update rejection, unchanged executable/PID, managed admin UI, and shutdown. CI also caught and verified fixes for protected-directory swaps on macOS and post-exit HTTP connection resets on Windows.

The attached npm tarball is the same artifact published to npm. Backend assets are available in the separate studio-v0.2.13-magpie.1 release.

releases.name: AI Studio 0.2.13-magpie.1 — Plugin-managed updates
releases.body:
AI Studio backend based on upstream v0.2.13, managed exclusively by the Magpie plugin.

- Disable online updates in the backend on macOS, Linux, and Windows. Update checks return local managed status; update installation returns HTTP 403 without changing files or restarting.
- Replace admin update controls with a bilingual message directing users to upgrade the plugin.
- Include five SHA-256-pinned platform archives, upstream MIT license, checksums, and reproducible build metadata.

Source: upstream commit a784c5193b3ba5c4894d536b2f4cd73e87f99475 plus patches/studio-managed.patch. Build instructions: docs/studio-release.md.

These are backend assets consumed by magpie-gemini-web v0.5.2, not the npm plugin package.
